availability.note: GAC AU spec page lists Premium and Luxury; AU model page offers ordering with $1,000 deposit, Q4 2026 campaign live

listPrice.note: CarExpert: $31,990 'before on-road costs' in words; CarsGuide price page (https://www.carsguide.com.au/gac/aion-ut/price/2026) gives the same MSRP excluding stamp duty. GAC's own AU site quotes only a Q4 2026 campaign drive-away (Premium from $31,990, orders 1 Oct-31 Dec 2026); RRP national drive-away per CarExpert review is $32,990, below the app's computed Vic drive-away ($34,214) because it is a flat national figure, so no back-out used

batteryKwh.note: GAC Europe: 'Net capacity 60 kWh (Gross: 62 kWh)', same 215/55 R17 car; EV Database agrees 60 usable / 62 nominal. Held 58 was wrong

rangeKm.note: GAC AU spec 'WLTP 430km'; GAC Europe WLTP combined 430km on the same 17-inch wheel

consumptionKwhPer100km.note: WLTP rated 164 Wh/km (EV Database); CarExpert quotes claimed 16.4kWh/100km. Battery-to-range gives 14.0, 17% off, within tolerance (rated figure includes charging losses)

bootLitresSeatsUp.note: 321L to the lower window (cover convention); GAC AU spec 'standard volume block method' 321/689. EU 440/1,600 is a different (to-roof) method

bootLitresSeatsDown.note: 689L seats folded to the lower window; matches GAC AU spec

towKg.note: EV Database: no tow hitch, braked 0kg; GAC AU spec lists no towing capacity

warrantyYears.note: 8yr/unlimited km vehicle warranty; only the 5yr roadside is conditional on GAC-network servicing

insuranceAnnual.note: anchored to byd-dolphin-premium $1,400 at $36,990 and mg-4-urban-54 $1,300 at $32,735; Luxury +$100 for the $4,000 step

depreciationCurve.note: one GAC brand curve shared with gac-aion-v: steeper than mainstream default for a new brand with no AU resale history, ~30 dealers and repeated drive-away campaigns (launch $30,990 d/a, Q4 2026 $31,990 d/a)
